features.name: Unified_Stylesheet
features.purpose: Gives every page of the site one consistent visual presentation so the site reads as a single coherent reference work rather than a marketing site, while sharing a few brand cues with the Spec4 app.

invocation.trigger: A reader opens or navigates to any page on the site

inputs.name: page content
inputs.description: The prose, code samples, tables, figures, and navigation links that make up a given page

inputs.name: system color scheme preference
inputs.description: The reader's device-level preference for a light or dark reading scheme

inputs.name: viewport width
inputs.description: The width of the reader's window or screen, used to decide when wide content needs to scroll

inputs.name: current section identifier
inputs.description: Which of the three main sections the current page belongs to, so navigation can mark it as active

outputs.primary: A visually consistent rendering of the page
outputs.schema_notes: Every page shows the same wordmark, navigation, typography choices, table behavior, code presentation, figure treatment, and color scheme rules; only content differs between pages

success_criteria: All thirteen pages share identical navigation placement, wordmark treatment, and typography choices
The wordmark's two-color treatment is the only place blue appears on the site
Switching a device between light and dark reading preference changes the site's appearance without any control on the page
Wide tables and code samples scroll within their own bounded area instead of breaking the page layout on narrow screens
Figures appear at a consistent full-column width with a visible caption
The active section is visibly indicated in the navigation on every page in that section
No icons, card shapes, hero banners, shadows, gradients, animation, a second accent color, or analytics indicators appear anywhere on the site

failure_modes.mode: One or more pages render with different typography, spacing, or navigation than the rest
failure_modes.mitigation: Apply the same shared presentation rules to every page rather than page-specific overrides

failure_modes.mode: Dark reading scheme produces low-contrast or unreadable text
failure_modes.mitigation: Define paired light and dark colors for background and text that both meet clear readability at normal reading distance

failure_modes.mode: A wide table or long code sample overflows and breaks the page layout on a narrow screen
failure_modes.mitigation: Contain such content in a bounded, independently scrollable area

failure_modes.mode: A visible control for switching color scheme appears, contradicting the no-toggle guarantee
failure_modes.mitigation: Drive the scheme purely from the reader's system-level preference with no on-page control

failure_modes.mode: Excluded decorative elements (icons, shadows, gradients, animation, extra accent color, analytics) creep back in over time
failure_modes.mitigation: Treat the exclusion list as a standing constraint checked whenever the shared presentation is changed

nfr_goals: Every page loads and renders correctly without requiring any script to run
Pages remain fully readable and navigable on narrow viewports without horizontal breakage of the overall layout
Text and code remain readable at sufficient contrast in both light and dark reading schemes
The shared visual presentation can be updated once and take effect consistently across all pages
The site collects no analytics or tracking information about readers
Pages load quickly even on slow connections, given they contain no scripts, media playback, or heavy assets
